full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee, J: This criminal appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated the 29th day of October. 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 19816 of 2008 arising out of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Case No. 253 of 2008 pending in the Court of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka summarily rejecting the application moved, under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure challenging the order passed by the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal on 11-8-2008 rejecting the Naraji petition filed by the complainant against the final report submitted by the Investigating Officer on 10-5-2008. 

 2. On 6-4-2008, the appellant as informant lodged FIR with Kafrul Police Station DMP, Dhaka-against opposite party No. 2 and on the basis of the said FIR, Kafrul Police Station Case No.7 dated 6-4-2008 under section 11(Ga) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 (as amended, 2003) was started. The FIR reads as: 

 5. Mr SN Goswami, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that the High Court Division committed an error of law in not giving effect to the provision of section 203 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which reads that the Magistrate before whom a complaint is made or to whom it has been transferred may dismiss the complaint, if, after considering the statement on oath (if any) of the complainant and the result of the investigation or inquiry, if any, under section 202, finds in his judgment that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding with the case. He further contended that the learned Judges of the Division Bench of the High Court Division committed error of law in not considering totality of the facts and circumstances since no witness was present before him and, as such, erroneously found that no prima-facie case was made out. 

 6. Mr. Jahangir Alam, learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the State, submits that instead of filing an appeal as provided in the said Ain, the appellant informant filed this petition under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure which is not at all tenable in the eye of law. He further submits that the appellant informant became furious after receiving the notice of Talak and instituted the present case on some false, frivolous and concocted grounds and, as such, she failed to collect witnesses in support of her case and as such, the Investigating Officer (I/O) was compelled to submit final report. 

 12. The learned Judge (Bicharok) Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka has proper authority to decide whether the case should be sent for blither investigation by any other agency or he can ask for a report after holding a judicial enquiry. We, therefor, hold the view that the impugned order as well as the order dated 11-8-2008 passed by the learned Judge (Bicharok) Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka should be set-aside and the matter should be placed before the learned Judge (Bicharok) Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka for taking steps in the light of the observations made in this judgment and order.
